approval_basis: Repository owner asked to continue the refactor (working session 2026-09-21). No vocabulary key was added, renamed or removed; master.snapshot.json is byte-identical to v1.1.0.
release_kind: minor — adds compatible mappings (question-wording rules); no accepted value changed

changes.meaning: questions.skill_key may now be derived from College Board's question wording (skill_key_source = 'question_text'), applied after a College Board label and before any LLM-assigned key. Matching uses the normalised last sentence of the question.

evidence.method: P(skill | wording); a rule is used only at n>=5 and purity>=95%

rules_in_effect.key: which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase
which choice completes the text with the most logical transition
which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal
which choice most logically completes the text
which choice best states the main idea of the text
which choice best states the main purpose of the text
which choice best describes the overall structure of the text
which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement
which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole
which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole
which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement
which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text
which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example
which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the text
based on the texts both authors would most likely agree with which statement
which choice best describes data from the graph that support the researchers conclusion
which finding if true would most directly support the researchers hypothesis

evidence.counterexample: 'Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?' is 213 Boundaries / 208 Form, Structure, and Sense and is deliberately not a rule.

migration.dry_run: 49 rows changed: 8 previously NULL resolved, 41 source upgrades, 2 values corrected where an annotation contradicted College Board's wording
migration.validation: second run changed 0 rows; annotation_jsonb checksum unchanged; 14 unit tests

changes.rollback: git revert the resolver and re-run scripts/fill_skill_key.py --apply

changes.meaning: The bank-to-database match now reads the layout-based master bank (prose only, without graph axis numbers) and accepts a database row that has lost its question stem when its text equals the College Board passage.

evidence.before: 733 bank questions on 1,414 rows; 11 for review
evidence.after: 745 bank questions on 1,457 rows; 1 for review
evidence.safety: all 1,414 earlier pairs kept, 0 lost, 0 rows changed College Board ID, 0 collisions; on the 35 rows whose source upgraded to cb the previously inferred skill already equalled College Board's label

migration.result: 1,513 of 1,514 questions carry skill_key (cb 1,457; question_text 36; annotation 12; map 8); 1 left NULL

changes.reason: v1.1.0 put vocabulary/mappings/cb_skill_map.json in the hash lock. That file is a derived, regenerable artifact: its counts change on every matcher run and every new College Board export even when no rule's outcome changes, so hashing it would force a release per export. It is removed from the lock. The rules actually in effect are recorded in the ledger instead (VOC-0008), and backend/tests/test_skill_key.py fails if the shipped map yields an illegal skill. backend/app/pipeline/skill_key.py stays locked, as the other enforcement inputs are.
